question: Qutub Minar is of how many storeys?
solution:
The correct answer is __5__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Qutab-ud-din Aibak, the **first Muslim ruler of Delhi**, commenced the** construction of the Qutab Minar in 1200 AD**, but could only finish the basement. His successor, Iltutmish, added three more storeys, and in 1368, **Firoz Shah Tughlaq constructed the fifth and the last storey. Hence, Option 1 is correct.**
 
• **Qutab Minar **is a soaring, 73 m-high tower of victory, built-in 1193 by Qutab-ud-din Aibak immediately after the defeat of Delhi's last Hindu kingdom.
 
• The** first three storeys** are made of** red sandstone, the fourth and fifth storeys are of marble and sandstone. **At the foot of the tower is the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, the first mosque to be built in India.
 
• The **minaret is named after Qutb-ud-din Aibak**, or Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki, a Sufi saint.
 
• The development of architectural styles from **Aibak to Tughlak** is quite evident in the minar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Qutub Minar (or Qutab Minar) is a minaret and "victory tower" that forms part of the Qutb complex.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Mehrauli area of New Delhi, India.
 
• The height of Qutb Minar is 72.5 meters, making it the tallest minaret in the world built of bricks.
 
• The tower tapers, and has a 14.3 meters (47 feet) base diameter, reducing to 2.7 meters (9 feet) at the top of the peak. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• Qutub-Ud-Din Aibak of the Slave Dynasty laid the foundation of Minar in A.D. 1199.
 
• Iltutmish and Firoz Shah Tughlaq, who were Qutub-Ud-din-Aibak's successors, completed the construction of the entire tower.
